chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: Five years at the Round-Up Club
summary: Smith's band shrank from 13 pieces to 5 or 6 and played five years for country-and-western crowds at the all-White Round-Up Club.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah, tenor players. Both of them tenor players. They were good. They were good musicians. And then I picked up a trombone player who stayed with me for a while... All of them stayed with me. You can get good musicians as long as you've got something to do. And when I quit running out and playing them three and four nights a week down here in these towns, and carried a show and everything... Things got (?) and then we didn't have nowhere to play. But here... After they closed up the big hole here, where we'd worked five years, and I had to cut the band down from 13 pieces to 8 pieces, to 5 or 6 pieces. We worked down here at the Round-Up Club, about five years down

there. That's where I got the hay fever from, working down there in all that dust. The man was sprinkling all those soap chips all over the floor. There was always 2,000 people in the house every night. We'd play from 12 to 2 in the morning, and just two hours. It would get so dusty...
We worked down there about five years, and then the city closed them up, said they had too many fights in the place or something or other. Anyway, they got mad at the man and...

No, it wasn't no rough place. Wasn't nothin' but just mostly mediocre people went there. In other words, it was Country-and-Western people, that Country-and-Western music. And they had a White band that played the first part of the night, from 8 to 12, and they played the Country-and-Western. All of them had on big cowboy hats. Then the man would bring me on to play the other kind of music for the younger generation that liked every kind of music.
You were playing Jazz in there?
And was this an all-White place?
Yeah. Mmm-hmm. The old Round-Up Club. Yeah. All-White..
